effects: The signer's underlying ERC-20 (underlying(), e.g. USDC or WETH) leaves the wallet: amount rounded down to a multiple of rate() is pulled with safeTransferFrom, spending the signer's allowance to the wrapper.
The receiver `to` gets amount / rate() confidential tokens (cToken, 6 decimals), minted as an encrypted balance.
Dust below rate() is not taken (amount % rate stays with the signer).
formats.shown: "Shield <raw integer> underlying units to <to>", with the raw amount and the receiver as fields; neither the underlying token nor the cToken received is named.

findings.title: wrap shows the underlying amount as a raw integer with no token name or decimals.
findings.evidence: descriptor wrap field {"path":"amount","label":"Amount (underlying units)","format":"raw"}; case 1 (cWETH, 18 decimals) shows "Shield 1000000000000000000 underlying units" for 1 WETH. Code: ERC7984ERC20WrapperUpgradeable.wrap pulls roundedAmount of IERC20(underlying()) from msg.sender.
findings.fix: Split the descriptor per underlying (or per deployment) and use format tokenAmount with params.token set to that chain's underlying address, so the screen reads e.g. "Shield 1 WETH".

findings.title: wrap intent names neither the asset leaving nor the confidential token minted to the receiver.
findings.evidence: intent "Shield"; interpolatedIntent "Shield {amount} underlying units to {to}". Code mints FHE.asEuint64(amount / rate()) cTokens to `to` (ERC7984ERC20WrapperUpgradeable.wrap). For rate 1e12 (cWETH), 1e18 units become 1 cWETH, and the screen never says so.
findings.fix: Once the underlying is resolvable, use an intent like "Shield {amount} into confidential tokens for {to}"; add a label that says the receiver gets the confidential version.

effects: Up to `amount` (an existing encrypted handle the signer may use) of cTokens is burned from `from`, either the signer or a holder that made the signer an operator. If the balance is too low, 0 is burned.
The burned amount is made publicly decryptable, so the amount is revealed.
An unwrap request is recorded that later sends burned amount × rate() of the underlying ERC-20 to `to` when finalizeUnwrap runs.
formats.shown: "Request to unshield [Encrypted Amount] from <holder> to <receiver>", with holder, receiver and the encrypted amount as fields.

findings.title: unwrap does not say the burned amount becomes publicly decryptable.
findings.evidence: ERC7984ERC20WrapperUpgradeable._unwrap: FHE.makePubliclyDecryptable(unwrapAmount_); the screen only says "Request to unshield [Encrypted Amount]".
findings.fix: Optionally mention in the intent that the unshielded amount becomes public, e.g. "Request to unshield (amount becomes public)".

findings.title: unwrap amount is an encrypted handle that most wallets will show as a placeholder.
findings.evidence: field `amount` uses definitions.encryptedAmount with encryption.fallbackLabel "[Encrypted Amount]"; case 2 shows "[Encrypted Amount]".
findings.fix: None in the descriptor; it depends on wallet FHE decryption support.

effects: Up to the encrypted input amount of cTokens is burned from `from` (the signer or a holder that made the signer an operator). If the balance is too low, 0 is burned.
The burned amount is made publicly decryptable.
An unwrap request is recorded that later sends burned amount × rate() of the underlying ERC-20 to `to` on finalizeUnwrap.
formats.shown: "Request to unshield [Encrypted Amount] from <holder> to <receiver>", with holder, receiver and encrypted amount; the input proof is hidden.

findings.title: unwrap with proof does not say the burned amount becomes publicly decryptable.
findings.evidence: ERC7984ERC20WrapperUpgradeable._unwrap: FHE.makePubliclyDecryptable(unwrapAmount_); screen in case 3 only says "Request to unshield".
findings.fix: Optionally mention in the intent that the unshielded amount becomes public.

effects: The wrapper sends unwrapAmountCleartext × rate() of the underlying ERC-20 to the recipient stored for the request (unwrapRequester). That recipient is not in calldata and is not necessarily the signer.
The request is deleted. None of the signer's assets leave; the cleartext is checked against the decryption proof.
formats.shown: "Finalize unshield of <amount> cUSDC", with the amount formatted in the cToken and the request id shown raw.

findings.title: finalizeUnwrap labels the amount in the confidential token, while the underlying ERC-20 is what gets delivered.
findings.evidence: field unwrapAmountCleartext tokenAmount with tokenPath "@.to" (the cToken); case 4 shows "Finalize unshield of 1 cUSDC". Code: SafeERC20.safeTransfer(IERC20(underlying()), to, unwrapAmountCleartext * rate()).
findings.fix: Relabel to make clear this is the unshielded amount paid out in the underlying token, e.g. "Unshielded amount (paid in underlying)", or use the underlying token constant per deployment.

findings.title: finalizeUnwrap recipient comes from storage and cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: ERC7984ERC20WrapperUpgradeable.finalizeUnwrap: address to = unwrapRequester(unwrapRequestId); no recipient on screen.
findings.fix: None possible from calldata; the request id stands in for it.

effects: Up to `amount` (an existing handle the signer may use) of the signer's cTokens moves to `to`. If the balance is too low, 0 moves.
Both parties are given ACL access to the transferred handle.
formats.shown: "Confidential transfer of [Encrypted Amount] to <receiver>", with amount and receiver fields.

findings.title: confidentialTransfer amount is encrypted and shows as a placeholder without wallet decryption.

effects: As operator of `from`, the signer moves up to `amount` of `from`'s cTokens to `to`. The operator right is time-bounded and is not reduced by this call.

effects: Up to `amount` of the signer's cTokens moves to `to`.
`to` is then called with onConfidentialTransferReceived(signer, signer, sent, data). If it returns encrypted false, the contract tries to refund the sent amount from `to`. The refund is best-effort.
formats.shown: "Confidential transfer of [Encrypted Amount] to <receiver>"; the callback data is hidden and the call to the receiver is not mentioned.

findings.title: confidentialTransferAndCall intent matches a plain transfer and hides the callback to the receiver.
findings.evidence: intent "Confidential transfer"; data field visible "never". Code: ERC7984Upgradeable._transferAndCall calls ERC7984Utils.checkOnTransferReceived(msg.sender, from, to, sent, data), then refunds on failure.
findings.fix: Use an intent like "Confidential transfer and call" so the signer knows the receiver contract runs code with hidden data.

effects: Up to the encrypted input amount of the signer's cTokens moves to `to`.
`to` is then called with the hidden data, with a best-effort refund if it returns false.
formats.shown: "Confidential transfer of [Encrypted Amount] to <receiver>"; the proof and callback data are hidden.

findings.fix: Use an intent like "Confidential transfer and call".

effects: Until timestamp `until` (inclusive), `operator` can transfer any amount of the signer's whole confidential balance and unwrap it to any address. This replaces any earlier expiry for that operator.
`until` = 0, or any past time, revokes the operator.
formats.shown: "Set <operator> authorization to expire on <date>", with operator and date fields.

findings.title: setOperator intent does not say the operator can move or unwrap the signer's whole confidential balance.
findings.evidence: intent "Set operator authorization"; ERC7984Upgradeable.isOperator returns true while block.timestamp <= _operators[holder][spender], and that gates confidentialTransferFrom* and _unwrap with no amount cap.
findings.fix: Use an intent like "Allow {operator} to move all your confidential tokens until {until}".

findings.title: setOperator with until=0 shows a 1970 date instead of saying the operator is revoked.
findings.evidence: case 14 screen: "Set 0x90F7… authorization to expire on 1970-01-01 00:00:00Z"; _setOperator stores 0, so isOperator is false from now on.
findings.fix: Add a label or note that a past date revokes the operator, or a dedicated rendering for 0 such as "Revoke".

effects: The given encrypted handle, which the signer must be allowed to use (for example their own balance), becomes publicly decryptable. Anyone can learn its value, and this cannot be undone.

findings.title: requestDiscloseEncryptedAmount cannot show which value (e.g. the signer's balance) the handle points to.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor; optionally say in the intent that disclosure is permanent.

effects: No asset moves. The contract checks the decryption proof and publishes an event pairing the handle with cleartextAmount.
